text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 18 in history:
1480 - Lucrezia Borgia, Italian noblewoman and illegitimate daughter of Pope Alexander VI, born.
1689 - British Chief Justice Judge George Jeffreys, died in the Tower of London. He presided over the "Bloody Assizes" following the Monmouth Rebellion of 1685,
1775 - Paul Revere rode from Charlestown to Lexington to warn the Massachussetts colonists of the arrival of British troops at the start of the War of American Independence.
1797 - Louis-Adolph Thiers, French statesman, born. He was the founder and first president of the Third Republic.
1820 - Franz von Suppe, Austrian composer of light operas, born. His most successful operas include "Leichte Kavallerie" and "Boccaccio".
1882 - Leopold Stokowski, orchestral conductor, born in London. Founder of the American Symphony Orchestra, he made three films, including Walt Disney's "Fantasia", with the Philadelphia Orchestra.
1906 - An earthquake struck San Francisco. The quake and resulting fires devastated the city, leaving over 200,000 people homeless and over 1,000 dead.
1909 - 15th century French heroine Joan of Arc was beatified at a ceremony at the Vatican.
1923 - Yankee Stadium, home of the New York Yankees baseball team, was opened.
1934 - The first launderette, the "Washateria", was opened at Fort Worth, Tex., by J.F. Cantrell.
1936 - Ottorino Respighi, Italian composer, died. Best known for his orchestral pieces such as the "Pines of Rome".
1942 - In World War Two, U.S. aircraft bombed Tokyo for the first time.

1945 - Ernie Pyle, one of the most famous war correspondents of World War Two, was killed by Japanese machine-gun fire on the island of Ii Shima in the Pacific. The 1945 film "G.I. Joe" was about his coverage of the Italian campaign.
1946 - The League of Nations dissolved itself and all its assets were handed over to the United Nations.
1949 - Southern Ireland (Eire) came into being with the passing of the Republic of Ireland Act.
1951 - France, West Germany, Italy and the three Benelux countries signed a treaty in Paris setting up the European Coal and Steel Community.
1954 - Gamal Abdel Nasser became prime minister of Egypt.
1955 - Albert Einstein, German born scientist died. He formulated the Theory of Relativity and won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1921.
1974 - Washington District Court conducting the Watergate proceedings issued a supoena on President Richard Nixon to produce tape recordings and other material demanded by the Special Prosecutor.
1978 - The U.S. Senate ratified the second Panama Canal Treaty, providing for the operation and defence of the canal until 1999.
1978 - Chilean President Augusto Pinochet announced a new cabinet composed for the first time since the 1973 coup mainly of civilians.
1980 - Rhodesia gained legal independence as Zimbabwe under President Canaan Banana.
1982 - The name of the capital of Zimbabwe was changed from Salisbury to Harare.
1983 - A suicide bomb shattered the U.S. embassy in Beirut, killing at least 63 people.
1988 - An Israeli court convicted John Demjanjuk of Nazi war crimes, saying he was the gas chamber operator "Ivan The Terrible" at the Treblinka death camp in World War Two.
1993 - In Pakistan, the government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif was dismissed by President Ishaq Khan.
1996 - Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) gunmen opened fire on a tourist bus in Cairo, killing 18 Greek tourists.
1996 - More than 100 Lebanese refugees, many of them women and children, were killed when Israeli artillery shells ripped into a crowded U.N. peacekeepers base where they were sheltering.

1996 - Britain withdrew an expulsion order on Saudi dissident Mohammed al-Masari, whose presence had threatened lucrative arms deals with Riyadh, and said he could stay in the country for four more years.
